Identity check first: "window" stresses WIN, so a rhyme needs a different consonant before that short-i vowel. "Widow" is close in sound but a different word; "window/window" would be identity, not rhyme.

Here is a labeled menu across the stability tiers. Pick by what you want line 4 to feel like; I won't pick one for you.

| Tier | Candidate | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Family | *in though* | voiced/unvoiced swap, soft landing |
| Family | *thin glow* | keeps the porch-light world |
| Additive | *winds blow* | extra consonant, still resolves |
| Subtractive | *win, though* | drops the d, conversational |
| Assonance | *sin, oh* | vowel-only, unresolved |
| Assonance | *gimme so* | loose, spoken |
| Consonance | *wander* | consonant frame, unstable |
| Mosaic | *been so slow* | multi-word, lands the waiting |
| Mosaic | *in the snow* | multi-word, season shift |
| Mosaic | *spin and go* | motion, leaving |

The menu leans unstable on purpose: he hasn't called, so a perfect rhyme may close the verse too neatly. The choice is yours by emotional intent.
